# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

1:- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
2:- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.
3:
4:### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`
5:
6:The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.
7:
8:`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`
9:
10:```yaml
11:# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
12:# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
13:validate:
14:  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
15:  next: load
16:load:
17:  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
18:  next: apply
19:apply:
20:  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
21:  govern: [ transaction ]
22:  next: save
23:save:
24:  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
25:  govern: [ transaction ]
26:  next: respond
27:respond:
28:  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
29:```
30:
31:```java
32:// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
33:public class ValidateOwner {
34:  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
35:    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
36:  }
37:}
38:public class LoadOwner {
39:  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
40:      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
41:    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
42:    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
43:    ownerOut.set(owner);
44:  }
45:}
46:public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
47:  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
48:    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
49:    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
50:  }
51:}
52:public class SaveOwner {
53:  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
54:    repository.save(owner);
55:  }
56:}
57:public class RespondWithOwner {
58:  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
59:    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
60:  }
61:}
62:```
63:
64:`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`
65:
66:```yaml
67:handle:
68:  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
69:```
70:
71:```java
72:public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
73:  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
74:      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
75:    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
76:  }
77:}
78:```
79:
80:### Step wiring
81:
82:Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
83:point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
84:method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
85:`method:`.
86:
87:- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
88:  as `@Parameter T`.
89:- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
90:  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
91:  branch; not calling it short-circuits.
92:
93:### Function parameters
94:
95:Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:
96:
97:- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
98:- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
99:- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
100:  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
101:  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
102:- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
103:  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.
104:
105:### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`
106:
107:Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
108:into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):
109:
110:- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
111:- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
112:  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
113:- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
114:  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.
115:
116:### Naming
117:
118:Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
119:absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
120:publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
121:`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).
122:
123:Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
124:responder. Steps in between work with entities.
125:
126:### Request body and validation
127:
128:- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
129:  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
130:  first step publishes it as a variable.
131:- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
132:  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
133:  invalid body can return 400.
134:
135:### Transactions
136:
137:`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
138:listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
139:the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.
140:
141:### Errors
142:
143:Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
144:Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
145:`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
146:`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
147:anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.
148:
149:### Security
150:
151:Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:
152:
153:```yaml
154:composition:
155:  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
156:```
157:
158:- Full reference: https://officefloor.net/llms.txt

content.text:
Stewards can now reopen a closed period, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it behaves**
- Only a steward can reopen. Anyone else gets "Only a steward can reopen a period" in the period's error element, and nothing is stored or written to the audit file.
- Reopening a period that doesn't exist or isn't closed is refused the same way. In the test, a second reopen is refused because the period is already open.
- A successful reopen sets the period back to open and clears its saved closing total. It then writes `PERIOD_REOPENED sheet=<id> by=<user> period=<name>` to the audit file.
- After reopening, the period's due-total is worked out again from its claims' current figures. Claims already put on a statement keep their saved amounts. I didn't change how claims are shown: the existing screen already shows those figures, even while the period is closed.

**What changed**
- **Server:** a new endpoint `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{periodName}/reopen`, in a YAML file next to the close one. It has two new steps, `ReopenPeriod` (the steward check and the reopen) and `AuditPeriodReopened`, plus a `reopen` method on `PeriodStore`. It reuses the close endpoint's request-body and response steps. No database migration was needed, because the existing `closed` and `closed_total` columns cover it.
- **Front end:** `features/periods/list.slot.tsx` has a new Reopen button (`period-reopen`) next to Close. Both buttons now share one action, so the period's error element (`period-error`) is cleared whenever the next action on that row is taken.
